title: Isolation, culture and transplantation of female germline stem cells from neonatal and prepubertal mice
protocol: Sacrifice mice and remove ovaries.
Place ovaries in a 60 mm glass dish containing D-Hank’s on ice.
Wash ovaries in 10 ml PBS.
Remove adherent tissue using fine forceps.
Transfer cleaned ovaries to another glass dish containing 50 μl D-Hank’s on ice.
Cut ovaries into small pieces with surgical scissors.
Transfer ovarian pieces to a 15 ml tube containing 5 ml digestion solution I.
Incubate in a 37 °C water bath with gentle agitation for approximately 20 minutes.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Wash the cells with 5 ml of D-Hank’s twice.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet by repeated pipetting with 5 ml of digestion solution II.
Place the suspension in a 37 °C water bath for 15 minutes and gently agitate to achieve a single cell suspension.
Terminate trypsin activity by adding 500 μl FBS.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 g for 5 minutes at room temperature (RT).
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in STO cell medium and remove cell clumps by passing the suspension through a 70 μm nylon cell strainer.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 g for 5 min at RT.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet by repeated pipetting with FGSC culture medium.
Incubate the goat anti-rabbit IgG microbeads (2 μl) and rabbit polyclonal MVH or Fragilis antibody (1 μl) in 200 μl PBS at 37°C for 30 minutes with gentle agitation.
Separate the mixture by magnetic bead separator to collect MVH or Fragilis microbeads, then discard the supernatant and resuspend the microbeads in 200 μl PBS.
Remove the FGSC medium by centrifugation (300 g for 5 min) for cell purification.
Wash cells twice with PBS and then resuspend the cells in 100 μl PBS.
Label cells by adding 100 μl MVH or Fragilis microbeads to a 2 ml microtube.
Incubate the mixture for 30 minutes at room temperature (RT) with gentle agitation.
Place the microtube containing the mixture in a magnetic bead separator for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant, wash cells by adding 0.5–1 ml PBS twice.
Resuspend the MVH+ or Fragilis+ cells separated by the magnetic bead separator by repeatedly pipetting the cell pellet with 300 μl FGSC medium.
Transfer MVH+ or Fragilis+ cells and FGSC medium onto a mitotically inactivated STO cell monolayer attached to 0.1% gelatin-coated culture wells (800–1200 MVH+ or Fragilis+ cells per well).
Culture the cells at 37 °C in 5% CO2.
Slowly add 300 μl fresh FGSC medium to each well on day 2.
On day 4, slowly remove half of the medium from each well and slowly add 300 µl fresh FGSC medium to well.
On day 6, slowly remove the medium from the wells and slowly add 300 µl fresh FGSC medium to each well.
Aspirate the supernatant from the wells and slowly add 200 µl PBS to each well to wash the cells once.
Add 50 µl 0.05% (wt/vol) trypsin/EDTA to the wells for detaching the cells and incubate at RT for 1 minute.
Add 200 µl STO cell medium and dissociate the MVH+ or Fragilis+ cells by repeated pipetting to achieve a single cell suspension.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 minutes at RT.
Discard the supernatant, resuspend the MVH+ or Fragilis+ cells in 300 µl FGSC medium, seed in one well of a 24-well plate containing a STO cell monolayer and incubate at 37 °C in 5% CO2.
Check the culture plates the next morning after subculture and exchange the medium if floating cell fragments are observed under a microscope.
Change the medium daily and passage cells as described in steps 15–18 onto freshly prepared plates containing a STO cell monolayer.
Gently pipette to detach FGSCs from the STO cell monolayer for expansion.
Seed FGSCs (0.5 × 10^6) in one well of a 6-well plate containing a STO cell monolayer and passage cells every 3–5 days at 1:2–1:3 split ratios.
Freeze FGSCs as soon as they grow to 3 confluent wells of a 24-well plate.
Rinse the 24 or 6 well plate containing the FGSCs with PBS twice.
Add trypsin/EDTA to the cells and digest for 1–2 minutes.
Add STO cell medium to stop the digestion, then collect the cells.
Pellet cells by centrifugation at 300 g for 5 minutes at room temperature, and remove the medium.
Slowly add freshly prepared cell-freezing medium to the pellet and carefully resuspend the cells (1 ml per vial and 3 confluent wells of a 24-well plate per vial).
Place the vials in a freezing vessel, cool to 4 °C for 1 hour, -20 °C for 2 hours, then -80 °C for 6 hours or overnight.
Transfer the vials to liquid nitrogen the next day for long-term storage.
Prepare a 15 ml tube with 10 ml STO cell medium prewarmed to 37 °C.
Take the vial directly from liquid nitrogen and immerse in a 37 °C water bath until the cells are completely thawed.
Sterilize the vial with 70% ethanol and transfer to a clean bench.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 minutes at RT after carefully transferring the cells to the prepared tube with STO cell medium, then remove the supernatant.
Gently resuspend the cells in FGSC medium by repeated pipetting.
Transfer the resuspended cells to prepared plates (mitotically inactivated STO cell monolayers attached to 0.1% gelatin-coated culture wells).
Change the medium the next morning.
Passage FGSCs into two wells of a 6 well plate and culture for 48 hours.
Aspirate the supernatant after culturing.
Add 1 ml fresh FGSC medium and colcemid at a 0.1 μg/ml final concentration to the cells.
Incubate for at least 3 hours after adding the medium and colcemid.
Remove the medium from FGSC cultures.
Digest with trypsin to achieve a single cell suspension.
Transfer cells into a 15 ml tube.
Centrifuge at 450 g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Hypotonically treat cells with prewarmed 75 mM KCl for 15 minutes.
Fix cells in methanol:acetic acid (3:1) for 30 minutes.
Air-dry fixed cells.
Stain cells with DAPI.
Aspirate FGSC medium and wash cells twice with PBS.
Fix FGSCs with 4% PFA solution.
Detect ALP activity according to the manufacturer’s instructions from the kit.
Remove the medium and wash FGSCs cultured in a 6 well plate twice with PBS.
Place the culture plate on ice.
Add 400 µl Trizol reagent per well.
Pipette Trizol across the surface of the well and scrape the surface to ensure complete lysis.
Transfer Trizol and cell lysates to a 1.5 ml eppendorf tube.
Isolate total RNA according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Quantitate total RNA by spectrophotometric analysis.
Qualify total RNA by visualization on a 1% agarose gel.
Perform reverse transcription and PCR using primers for Oct4, MVH, Fragilis, Dazl, and Stella.
Electrophorese the PCR products in a 1–2% agarose gel.
Inject busulfan at 30 mg/kg body weight into female recipient mice.
Inject cyclophosphamide at 120 mg/kg body weight into female recipient mice.
Wait 3–7 days after busulfan and cyclophosphamide injections for transplantation.
Anesthetize recipients with a sodium pentobarbitone injection at 45 mg/kg body weight intraperitoneally.
Disinfect the abdominal surface using 75% ethanol.
Open the abdominal cavity carefully.
Locate the Y-shaped uterus to find the ovaries.
Follow the uterus and oviduct posterior to the kidneys.
Identify small bean-shaped ovaries caudal to the kidneys in the lower abdominal cavity.
Gently hold an ovary with forceps.
Inject an ovary at 1–2 sites using a glass pipette with a 45 μm tip.
Transplant a 6 µl single-cell suspension of ~ 1 × 10^4 FGSCs into each recipient ovary.
Mate recipients with 8-week-old male mice after transplantation for ≥ 35 days.
Extract genomic DNA from the tail of 8-day-old offspring.
Use GFP specific primers for PCR detection of GFP.
Digest the genomic DNA from the above step with EcoR I.
Depurinate the digested genomic DNA.
Denature the depurinated DNA.
Neutralize the denatured DNA.
Perform prehybridization.
Hybridize samples using GFP specific primers.
Detect a GFP signal in samples by Southern blot analysis.
